judgments.reasoning_cat1: A gender-neutral reading convention using ordinary language ('may connote a masculine gender ... intended to include all employees'); nothing here has two competing operative meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is an interpretive aid that harmonises with every substantive provision (e.g. 2-A.1's 'Route men', 4-A.3's 'No man'); no operative term contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'as agent of the following individual Publishers' and 'binding upon each of the said individual Publishers or its successor' leaves 'successor' wholly undefined, a term with real reach in a multiemployer setting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Section 19, which says the Agreement 'was negotiated individually ... and shall be treated ... as an individual agreement,' creating a genuine question whether this is one association-wide contract or two.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The boundary is fixed only 'approximately' — 'a radius of approximately fifty miles' and 'bounded approximately as follows' — so the outer edge of the Metropolitan Area cannot be applied with precision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Metropolitan Area' is load-bearing throughout (2-E.1, 2-E.2(e), 3-E, 12-A.1, 21-D V), and the Carlstadt/Newspoint and over-the-road provisions depend on where the line falls.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated list of covered operations with an internal exception ('Collectors, except in the case of any Publisher using a billing system operated through the auditing department') invites expressio unius arguments about work not named.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-B immediately adds a catch-all for 'any other operation,' and 2-C, 2-H.2 and the Carlstadt jurisdiction minutes all pull on the same unit boundary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition of 'dealer' is introduced by 'i.e.' but gives only an example, and the text is broken ('or in the same manner as present practice'), leaving the exception's scope unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'no regular situation holder ... shall be laid off solely as a result' tracks 2-E.2(i) and 3-D.4 but sits against the broad layoff right in 3-D.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is the paradigm general catch-all after an enumerated list: 'any other operation, occupation or branch of work which is now being performed exclusively by employees for whom the Union is now the recognized bargaining representative' — 'exclusively' and 'now' both bite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 2-A.1's specific list and 2-H.1's preservation of other unions' mailroom jurisdiction, the reach of the catch-all is genuinely contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'new mechanical devices ... to perform or aid in the performance of any of the operations included in the bargaining unit' is broad but its terms are ordinary; 'aid in' is the soft spot.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pushes against 3-D.4/3-D.5, which contemplate automated systems creating excess situations, and against 2-H.1's preservation of other unions' jurisdiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat recognition of named terminals as delivery points; no term carries two meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2-E.1 and 2-E.2; nothing in the instrument contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'to areas where for any reason distribution is interrupted' is open-ended, though the operative grant is a simple permission.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with 2-A.1's 'Canada men' and 3-C; no competing provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final saving clause ('this shall not be deemed to curtail the right to make substitution for a bus or railroad now being used') cuts against the prohibition just stated, and 'existing means or methods' is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-E.2(h) lets a Publisher 'at any time increase, decrease, or discontinue any over-the-road trucking and employ railroad, aircraft, or any other form of transportation,' which is hard to square with the approval requirement here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence of plain permission that employees 'may be required to operate tractor-trailer trucks.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the gateway to the rest of 2-E.2 and to 22-D's Times-specific gloss, but standing alone it is consistent with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'who are qualified, in order of seniority' could mean qualified-then-seniority or seniority-among-qualified, a small but real ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to Section 4-B, which governs bidding for vacant situations rather than selection of drivers, so the cited mechanism does not obviously fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A reasonable number of employees' is a vague quantity with no boundary supplied anywhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision defines or caps training opportunities; it sits comfortably beside 2-E.2(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'This article is intended only to establish terms and conditions for operating tractor-trailer trucks' is a scope-limiting sentence that fights with the broad grant in the same paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'The Publishers shall be free to select any runs' is in tension with 2-E.2(e)'s requirement that transfer points be 'agreed upon by the parties' and with 3-E's methods-and-extent freeze.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'as near the limits of such areas as practical' is a vague standard, and the carve-out for runs 'specifically dealt with in (e)(1)' must be read against it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-D Point Two expressly directs that paragraph (e) 'will be construed as if it reads as follows' for The Times, substituting a 250-mile/two-stop regime — a direct textual override.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Albany or any other city designated by the Publisher outside the Metropolitan Area' is broad but operationally clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-D(i) excepts common-carrier runs beyond 250 miles or with more than two stops, which qualifies this through-driving rule for The Times.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: OCR damage aside, the mechanics ('presently recognized exchange points at or near the city line') are concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2-E.2(g) and 3-E; no contradicting term located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short conditional permission; 'jurisdictional dispute with another union' is a recognised term of art here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels 2-H.1 and 9-B's jurisdictional-conflict carve-outs, and 22-D(vii) uses the same escape; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'to the extent that such forms of transportation may now be employed' is an undefined baseline qualifying an otherwise unlimited management right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-D Point (x) expressly stipulates that '(h) may not be invoked by The Times' to reassign nine-month runs to a common carrier, and 3-E freezes methods and extent — both cut against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'laid off solely as a result of the establishment of the run' turns entirely on 'solely,' a qualifier that routinely generates causation disputes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with 3-D.1's recognised right to lay off 'for economic or business reasons' and 3-D.2's expansive definition of those reasons.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed dollar bonus tied to a defined triggering event; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel in form to 3-Q's hi-lo bonus and consistent with the wage schedules in 13-A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow prohibition on contracting with another union as to inspectors and Return Department employees; terms are specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits beside 2-H.1's preservation of other unions' mailroom jurisdiction but does not contradict it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The tail 'present practice, however, excepted' swallows the rule without identifying what the practice is.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Similar 'present practice' savings appear in 3-G, 12-C and 5-N, so the pattern is consistent even if individually vague.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Conditions and methods of operation now prevailing ... shall not be disturbed' freezes an unspecified baseline, and the arbitration duty is conditioned on 'provided such other union or unions agree.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps 16-M.3's no-change-in-condition rule and cuts against the management rights in 3-B, 3-D.1 and 3-I.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'When full operations commence at an annex or a new or additional building' leaves 'full operations' undefined for a jurisdiction trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to 2-A and 2-B, and the Carlstadt (22-A) and Newspoint (21-D) jurisdiction memoranda set out different, plant-specific allocations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear reciprocal rule about assignment and inability to perform other operations; the double negative is awkward but not ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4-A.4 (competence) and 14-B (physical incapacity); no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is broken — 'shall be entitled to for work' is missing its verb (evidently 'to shape') — so the right created cannot be read off the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The default/restitution rule fits 2-A.1's 'Collectors' and 13-F/13-G on collections and shortages; no contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean prohibition with a stated exception for foremen and assistant foremen.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10 permits non-member 'half-day boys' to work 'in aid of and under the direction of a route man,' which sits awkwardly against this bar on non-covered employees performing Section 2 operations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'maximum Union security permissible under the Labor Management Relations Act ... to the extent embodied in Section 17' defines the obligation only by reference, so its content is uncertain on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 17-A.1 says the closed-shop language is reprinted 'for reference only and not as a part of this Agreement,' while 17-A.2 revives it automatically if law permits — a genuine tension with a clause that measures union security by Section 17.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite 30-day membership rule tied to regular situation holder status.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2-N.3's agency-fee mechanism for non-members and with 2-L.1; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading is 'Work on Sixth Shift' but the text addresses competence and the fifth shift, and the first sentence is corrupt ('employed to an the requirements'); the meaning cannot be read straight off it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nearly identical language appears in the italicised former 2-L reprinted in 17-A.1, which is declared 'not a part of this Agreement,' so the same words appear twice with opposite operative status.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One short flat prohibition; 'engage any person to aid him' is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10-B defines half-day boys as working 'in aid of and under the direction of a route man,' which requires reconciling but is employer-engaged rather than employee-engaged.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed, mechanical check-off procedure with fixed timing; nothing genuinely two-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The October 26, 1981 letter agrees 'to amend section 2-N.1 to provide for the checkoff of dues on a weekly or bi-weekly basis,' which supersedes the monthly mechanics on notice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory-compliance sentence with no operative discretion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors 17-B's separability approach; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cap — 'the amount payable per shift' shall not 'exceed 5% of the monthly dues payable by regular situation holders' — mixes per-shift and monthly measures, which can be read more than one way.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies to 'non-member extras and casuals' while 2-L.2 requires membership only of regular situation holders; the two fit together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the schedules shown in the last notice of such schedules to the Union' incorporates an unidentified external document, though the 46-pound cap is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-H prescribes Times bundle schedules including 'bundle weight of 42 pounds or more' and 37-46 pound loadings, which must be squared with the frozen schedules and the 46-pound ceiling.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A duty to publish a schedule; the content criteria are left open but the obligation is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Newspoint (21-D I) and 21-C.2 set specific load maxima that operate alongside these plant schedules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple posting and furnishing duty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallels 4-G's list-posting duty; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'unduly burdensome' is a vague standard with no metric, and the Publisher's counterpart trigger is the equally open 'newspaper operational conditions warrant it.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It routes to Section 16, consistent with the rest of the grievance architecture.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'unduly burdensome' and 'unduly difficult to serve' are undefined standards limiting an otherwise absolute management right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-M.3 forbids any 'change in condition' without the other party's prior consent, which is hard to reconcile with an unqualified right to determine wrapping, receipt points and dealer counts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'shall at their respective points personally supply all dealers and newsboys' is short and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2-D.2's Canada points; nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'as such Publisher may find necessary or desirable' is a subjective standard, and review is limited to whether the layoff 'was for economic or business reasons.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It collides with 3-D.4's flat ban on automation layoffs of listed holders, 2-E.2(i), 2-A.2 and 20-E.6's express waiver of layoff rights on the Bulldog phase-out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional clause that both invokes 'usual and ordinary sense' and sweeps in 'all reasons of an economic or business character' — self-referential and boundaryless.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is drafted precisely to control 3-D.1, and no other provision cuts across it except the automation carve-out in 3-D.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision requires employment of laid-off wholesaler employees while saying it 'shall in no way limit the Publisher's right to lay off pursuant to Section 3-D' — an internal pull that only the 15-day delay resolves.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers generally to 'Section 3-D' and to the methods-and-extent rules in 3-E/3-F, and 12-D.1 provides a separate financial-benefits regime for the same laid-off wholesaler employees.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such automated process or automated system shall be construed to include, among other such ... conveyor belts, wire-tying machines and the like' is a classic ejusdem generis list, and the 1981 list/1965 date pairing is odd.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The absolute no-layoff promise is difficult to reconcile with 3-D.1's recognised layoff right and 3-D.6's savings language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long and intricate but each step (declaration of excess, bidding under 4-B, assignment of starting time and days off) is specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The mechanism parallels 20-E.5's 'excess situation holder' regime for the Bulldog phase-out, which uses a different placement rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A stacked savings clause — 'as many regular situations as possible, subject to the terms of Sections 3-D.1 and 16 ... and other pertinent provisions thereof' — that preserves obligations while subordinating them to their own opposite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly points at 5-G and 3-D.1, two provisions that pull in opposite directions, so harmonising them is exactly the exercise it invites.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Methods and extent of direct delivery and combined delivery ... as they exist ... at the time of the effective date hereof are to be continued' freezes an undefined status quo and does not say what counts as a 'change.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-F gives the Publisher free choice on new routes, 2-E.2(h) lets it discontinue over-the-road trucking at will, and a side letter 'Clarification of Method and Extent' says the agreement 'prohibits the subcontracting of bargaining unit deliveries except as it may exist pursuant to the contract.'

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'new sections or new routes' is the whole battleground and is left undefined against existing routes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the direct counterweight to 3-E's freeze, and the two together determine when Joint Standing Committee approval is needed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Present practices' are frozen without identification, and 'good cause shown' is an open standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 12-C repeats this paragraph essentially verbatim, so the same rule appears twice in the instrument — redundancy that invites argument about whether they mean the same thing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'undue hardship or hazard,' 'excessive work tasks' and 'insofar as practicable' are three undefined standards in one paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The News side letter on 'Heaters, Bostrum Seats and Safety Equipment' adds equipment commitments that overlay the heater/defroster duty here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'coverage in the amount of $20,000, $50,000 beginning January 1, 1982' is punctuated so badly that the operative amounts and dates must be inferred, and the trigger ('assaults or other criminal conduct') is a general catch-all after a specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coverage overlaps the Welfare Fund (13-H) and the Times/News life insurance provisions (22-G), but no direct contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain management right to run either shift, with pay at the scale for the shift worked.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with 5-A and 5-B's shift definitions and 6-C's supervision rule; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'make every effort' and 'in so far as that may be practicable' are soft obligations immediately disclaimed by the closing proviso.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with 5-I's double-time rule for Sunday advance-section work, which it expressly does not disturb.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'at its then fair value' and 'no longer is fit for use' are valuation and condition standards with no mechanism, and the anti-discrimination proviso is open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3-K's own grievance route to the Joint Standing Committee; no competing provision located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is heavily corrupted and the two sentences point different ways — matter 'handled ... as the Publisher may direct' versus matter that 'shall be tied, handled and delivered by an extra crew' — with the dividing line drawn by three overlapping negative criteria.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-D V(c) disapplies the 'extra crew' requirement at Newspoint while citing it as 'Section 8-L,' a mis-citation of this very provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any other terms or conditions more favorable' is a broad general phrase trailing a specific wage-rate reference, and the long sentence loses its main verb in places.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the most-favoured-nation letters (pension/welfare letter; News memorandum ¶1.D) without contradicting them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of internal governance instruments closed by 'or rules of any character,' but the operative test ('in conflict with the provisions hereof') is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 17-B's separability clause and 17-C's spirit-and-letter clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'best efforts collectively and individually to promote the business and interests of the several Publishers' is a short, wholly unbounded standard — the kind of phrase courts routinely have to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits beside 16-N's no-strike clause and 17-C's spirit-and-letter clause without contradicting either.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'immediate family shall include' followed by an enumerated list plus 'legal dependents as defined by the Internal Revenue Code' uses 'include' — open or exhaustive is genuinely arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The three-day leave is conditioned on days falling in the regular work week, consistent with 5-G scheduling and 13-K paid leave.
